items.title: Total mass, total momentum, centre of mass, angular momentum, torque, kinetic energy, power and work of a particle model in an inertial frame
items.statement:
Fix a model of the force branch [[post-cm02-force-superposition]]: $N\ge1$
particle labels with fixed masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$
([[post-cm01-worldlines]] clause (v)), a time window $I_{0}\subseteq\mathbb
R$, an open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ with its collision
set removed when the model's force law is singular there
([[def-cm01-configuration]]), and a force map
$$F:I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}\longrightarrow(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$$
with the standing continuity and state-local-Lipschitz hypotheses of clause
(iii) of that postulate. Fix one inertial frame of the model with adapted
coordinates $(t,x)$ ([[post-cm01-frames]]), and let $J\subseteq I_{0}$ be an
interval with nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]). All sums below range over
$i=1,\dots,N$ ([[lem-finite-sum-laws]]), and $u\times v$, $\langle u,v\rangle$
and $\lVert u\rVert_{2}$ are the cross product, the Euclidean inner product and
the Euclidean norm on $\mathbb R^{3}$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]],
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

**(a) Curve families and motions.** A **curve family** of the model is a map
$x:J\to Q$, $x=(x_{1},\dots,x_{N})$, of class $C^{2}$ on $J$
([[def-cm01-velocity-acceleration]]); its **coordinate velocities** are
$w_{i}:=x_{i}'$ on $J$, written $w=(w_{1},\dots,w_{N}):J\to(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$.
A curve family is a **motion** of the model when
$$m_{i}\ddot x_{i}(t)=F_{i}\bigl(t,x(t),w(t)\bigr)\qquad(i=1,\dots,N,\ t\in J),$$
the notion of clause (c) of [[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]. Every quantity of
this definition is defined for an arbitrary curve family; the balance theorems
of this page state which of their properties use the equations of motion.
Along a curve family the force map is evaluated at $(t,x(t),w(t))\in
I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$; when the model invokes the
external-plus-pair presentation of clause (i) of [[post-cm02-interactions]],
the maps $F_{i}^{\mathrm{ext}}$ and $F_{ij}$ are evaluated at their declared
arguments on the motion's state graph, where the presentation is an identity
for $F_{i}$.

**(b) Total mass, total momentum, centre of mass, relative positions.** Define
$$M:=\sum_{i}m_{i}>0,\qquad p_{i}:=m_{i}w_{i},\qquad P(t):=\sum_{i}p_{i}(t),\qquad X(t):=M^{-1}\sum_{i}m_{i}x_{i}(t),\qquad \rho_{i}:=x_{i}-X.$$
Here $p_{i}$ is the **momentum** of label $i$, $P$ the **total momentum**, $X$
the **centre of mass** and $\rho_{i}$ the **relative position** of label $i$.
The dimensions are $[M]=\mu$, $[p_{i}]=[P]=\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$ (read in
$\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$) and $[X]=[\rho_{i}]=\ell$
([[def-cm01-units]]). Since $x_{i}$ is $C^{2}$, each $p_{i}$ is $C^{1}$ and
each of $P$, $X$, $\rho_{i}$ is differentiable, as a finite sum of
differentiable curves ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]); write
$$V:=X'$$
for the **centre-of-mass velocity**. The algebraic identities
$\sum_{i}m_{i}\rho_{i}=0$, $P=MV$ and the splitting of the kinetic sum
$\sum_{i}m_{i}\lVert w_{i}\rVert_{2}^{2}$ are proved in the kinetic-splitting
theorem of this page; they are not part of this definition.

**(c) Angular momentum, torque, internal torque sum.** Let a **reference
curve** $o:J\to\mathbb R^{3}$ of class $C^{1}$ be given: a point about which
moments are taken, allowed to move (a constant map $o\equiv o_{0}$ is the
fixed-origin case). Define the **angular momentum about $o$** and the **total
torque about $o$** by
$$J_{o}(t):=\sum_{i}\bigl(x_{i}(t)-o(t)\bigr)\times p_{i}(t),\qquad T_{o}(t):=\sum_{i}\bigl(x_{i}(t)-o(t)\bigr)\times F_{i}\bigl(t,x(t),w(t)\bigr),$$
with dimensions $[J_{o}]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$ (read in
$\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{2}\,\mathrm s^{-1}$) and
$[T_{o}]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ (read in $\mathrm N\,\mathrm m$). When the
model invokes the external-plus-pair presentation of clause (i) of
[[post-cm02-interactions]], define in addition the **external torque** and the
**internal torque sum**
$$T_{o}^{\mathrm{ext}}(t):=\sum_{i}\bigl(x_{i}(t)-o(t)\bigr)\times F_{i}^{\mathrm{ext}}\bigl(t,x_{i}(t),w_{i}(t)\bigr),\qquad I(t):=\sum_{i<j}\bigl(x_{i}(t)-x_{j}(t)\bigr)\times F_{ij}\bigl(t,x_{i}(t),x_{j}(t),w_{i}(t),w_{j}(t)\bigr).$$
The sum $I$ does not involve $o$; it is defined whenever the pair
presentation is declared. The identity $T_{o}=T_{o}^{\mathrm{ext}}+I$ uses the
antisymmetry $F_{ji}=-F_{ij}$ of clause (ii)1 of that postulate to reindex the
ordered pairs and is proved as step 1.1 of the angular-momentum balance of
this page.

**(d) Kinetic energy, power, work.** Define the **kinetic energy** and the
**power of the total force** along the curve family by
$$K(t):=\frac12\sum_{i}m_{i}\lVert w_{i}(t)\rVert_{2}^{2},\qquad \mathcal P(t):=\sum_{i}\bigl\langle F_{i}\bigl(t,x(t),w(t)\bigr),\,w_{i}(t)\bigr\rangle,$$
of dimensions $[K]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ (read in joules) and
$[\mathcal P]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-3}$ (read in watts), and for
$t_{0}<t_{1}$ in $J$ the **work of the total force** over $[t_{0},t_{1}]$ by
$$W([t_{0},t_{1}]):=\int_{t_{0}}^{t_{1}}\mathcal P(t)\,dt,$$
of dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ (read in joules); $\mathcal P$ is
continuous on $J$ because $F$, $x$ and $w$ are continuous, so the Riemann
integral exists ([[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]], see the page
`the-riemann-integral`). The **potential energy** is not defined by this item:
it belongs to the potential branch of the model and is defined in the
potential-and-mechanical-energy item of this page.

**(e) Frame and reference-point dependence.** The quantities $p_{i}$, $P$,
$X$, $\rho_{i}$, $V$, $K$, $\mathcal P$ and $W$ are read in the one inertial
frame fixed above, and $J_{o}$, $T_{o}$, $T_{o}^{\mathrm{ext}}$, $I$ are read
about the reference curve $o$ in that frame. They are not invariant under a
change of frame or reference point: their transformation laws under a change
of inertial frame are stated and proved in the frame-transformation item of
this page, and every conservation statement involving them names the frame
and the reference point in which it is made.

**(f) Status.** This item is a definition: it introduces symbols, their
domains, regularity, dimensions and frame dependence from the model's data.
It adopts no force law beyond the force branch already fixed, asserts no
balance of any of these quantities and records no measured value.
items.strategy: A definition: it fixes the total mass, total momentum, centre of mass, relative positions, angular momentum about a reference curve, total/external/internal torques, kinetic energy, power and work of a force model in one inertial frame, with domains, regularity, dimensions and frame dependence; it adopts no balance and no measured value.
items.physical_scope: Vocabulary and dimension conventions for the mechanical quantities of a force model in one inertial frame: the total mass, total momentum, centre of mass, relative positions and centre-of-mass velocity; the angular momentum, total torque, external torque and internal torque sum about a reference curve; the kinetic energy, the power of the total force and the work over a time interval. The item defines these symbols from the model's particles and force map and fixes their frames; it asserts no balance, no conservation law and no measured value.

references.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 1.3, printed pages 5-9 (PDF pages 11-15): the total mass M and centre of mass R = sum_i m_i r_i / M, the total momentum P = sum_i p_i, the total angular momentum L = sum_i L_i, the total kinetic energy T = (1/2) sum_i m_i rdot_i^2, and the definitions F^ext and tau^ext = sum_i r_i x F_i^ext

K. K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part CM: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), Section 1.3, chapter pages 6-10 (PDF pages 10-14): the definitions T = m v^2 / 2 (Eq. 1.19), the angular momentum L = r x p of a particle (Eq. 1.31), the total angular momentum of a system (Eq. 1.36), and the torque tau = r x F (Eq. 1.34)

items.title: Total momentum equals total mass times centre-of-mass velocity, and the kinetic energy splits into centre-of-mass and relative parts (two-body reduced mass)
items.statement:
Adopt the force model, the inertial frame and the notation of
[[def-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-momenta]]: masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, a
curve family $x:J\to Q$ of class $C^{2}$ on an interval $J$ with nonempty
interior, coordinate velocities $w_{i}=x_{i}'$, and the quantities
$$M=\sum_{i}m_{i},\qquad P=\sum_{i}m_{i}w_{i},\qquad X=M^{-1}\sum_{i}m_{i}x_{i},\qquad \rho_{i}=x_{i}-X,\qquad V=X',\qquad K=\frac12\sum_{i}m_{i}\lVert w_{i}\rVert_{2}^{2}.$$
Then:

1. $P=MV$ on $J$, that is $X'=M^{-1}P$, and the identities
   $$\sum_{i}m_{i}\rho_{i}=0,\qquad \sum_{i}m_{i}\rho_{i}'=0$$
   hold on $J$;
2. for every $t\in J$,
   $$K(t)=\frac12M\lVert V(t)\rVert_{2}^{2}+\frac12\sum_{i}m_{i}\lVert\rho_{i}'(t)\rVert_{2}^{2};$$
3. if $N=2$, then with $r:=x_{1}-x_{2}$ and $\mu:=m_{1}m_{2}/M$ one has, for
   every $t\in J$,
   $$K(t)=\frac12M\lVert V(t)\rVert_{2}^{2}+\frac12\mu\lVert r'(t)\rVert_{2}^{2}.$$

The statement is an identity for the stated curves and masses in the fixed
frame; it uses no equation of motion, no property of the force map and no
conservation claim. The values are frame-dependent; the transformation laws
are the frame-transformation item of this page.
items.strategy: A conditional identity: apply the mathematical centre-of-mass and kinetic-splitting theorem to the model's curves and masses, translate its notation into the model's momentum and kinetic energy, and read off the two-body reduced-mass form; no equation of motion and no force structure is used.
items.physical_scope: The algebraic identities of a curve family of a force model in one inertial frame: the total momentum is the total mass times the centre-of-mass velocity, the mass-weighted relative positions sum to zero together with their derivatives, and the total kinetic energy equals the centre-of-mass kinetic energy plus the mass-weighted relative kinetic energy, with the two-body reduced-mass form. The result is a conditional identity for the model's masses and curves and asserts no conservation law, no force structure and no measured value.

references.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 1.3, Eqs. (1.15) and (1.22)-(1.23), printed pages 6-8 (PDF pages 12-14): the centre of mass R = sum_i m_i r_i / M and the kinetic-energy decomposition T = (1/2) M Rdot^2 + (1/2) sum_i m_i rtilde_i^2

K. K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part CM: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), Section 3.4, Eqs. (3.30)-(3.35), printed pages 40-42: the centre-of-mass and reduced-mass construction for two bodies

items.title: Total momentum balance and centre-of-mass equation for a model with antisymmetric pair forces
items.statement:
Adopt the force model and one inertial frame of
[[def-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-momenta]], and suppose in addition that the
model invokes the external-plus-pair presentation of clause (i) of
[[post-cm02-interactions]],
$$F_{i}(t,z)=F_{i}^{\mathrm{ext}}(t,x_{i},v_{i})+\sum_{j\ne i}F_{ij}(t,x_{i},x_{j},v_{i},v_{j}),$$
with the antisymmetry clause (ii)1 of that postulate,
$F_{ij}(t,x_{i},x_{j},v_{i},v_{j})=-F_{ji}(t,x_{j},x_{i},v_{j},v_{i})$ on the
common domain. Let $x:J\to Q$ be a motion of the model on an interval $J$ with
nonempty interior, with quantities $M$, $P$, $X$, $V$ as in the definition,
and write
$$\sigma(t):=\sum_{i}F_{i}^{\mathrm{ext}}\bigl(t,x_{i}(t),w_{i}(t)\bigr)\qquad(t\in J)$$
for the **total external force along the motion**. Then:

1. $P$ is of class $C^{1}$ on $J$ and
   $$\dot P(t)=\sigma(t)\qquad(t\in J):$$
   the total momentum changes at the rate of the total external force, the
   internal pair forces cancelling in the sum;
2. if $\sigma\equiv0$ on $J$, then $P$ is constant on $J$ and $V=M^{-1}P$ is
   constant on $J$;
3. $X$ is of class $C^{2}$ on $J$ and
   $$M\,X''(t)=\sigma(t)\qquad(t\in J):$$
   the centre of mass obeys the equation of a single particle of mass $M$
   under the total external force.

The statement assumes the pair presentation and its antisymmetry; for a model
whose force map is not presented through such pairs it asserts nothing, and
the pair forces of the presentation need not be central (centrality is used
only in the angular-momentum balance of this page). No empirical content is
claimed.
items.strategy: A conditional deduction: evaluate the model's external-plus-pair presentation with antisymmetric pair forces along a motion, apply the mathematical momentum-balance identity, and derive the conservation criterion and the centre-of-mass equation from the definition's identities.
items.physical_scope: The momentum balance of a model that declares the external-plus-pair force presentation with antisymmetric pair forces: along every motion the total momentum changes at the rate of the total external force, it is constant on an interval exactly when the total external force vanishes there, and the centre of mass obeys the single-particle equation with the total mass and the total external force. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted force and interaction posts; it asserts no conservation for models without the antisymmetry presentation and no measured value.

references.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 1.3, Eqs. (1.12)-(1.16), printed pages 5-6 (PDF pages 11-12): F_i = sum_j F_ij + F_i^ext with F_ij = -F_ji, the cancellation of internal forces, Pdot = F^ext and M Rddot = F^ext

K. K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part CM: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), Section 1.3, Eqs. (1.29)-(1.30), chapter pages 8-9 (PDF pages 12-13): the decomposition F_k = sum F_kk' + F_k^(ext) and Pdot = F^(ext) after internal cancellation by the third law, valid in an inertial frame

R. Fitzpatrick, Classical Mechanics (University of Texas at Austin), Non-Isolated Systems, Eqs. (38)-(44): the internal-plus-external force decomposition, the summed balance and the cancellation of internal forces in pairs

items.title: Angular momentum balance about a fixed or moving reference point, the internal torque sum, and the centrality case
items.statement:
Adopt the force model and one inertial frame of
[[def-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-momenta]], and suppose that the model invokes
the external-plus-pair presentation of clause (i) of [[post-cm02-interactions]]
with the antisymmetry clause (ii)1 (as in the momentum balance of this page).
Let $x:J\to Q$ be a motion on an interval $J$ with nonempty interior and let
$o:J\to\mathbb R^{3}$ be a $C^{1}$ reference curve, with $J_{o}$,
$T_{o}$, $T_{o}^{\mathrm{ext}}$, $I$ and $P$ as in the definition. Then:

1. **Internal torque identity.** For every $t\in J$,
   $$\sum_{i}\bigl(x_{i}(t)-o(t)\bigr)\times\sum_{j\ne i}F_{ij}\bigl(t,x_{i}(t),x_{j}(t),w_{i}(t),w_{j}(t)\bigr)=I(t),\qquad\text{so}\qquad T_{o}(t)=T_{o}^{\mathrm{ext}}(t)+I(t);$$
2. **Balance.** $J_{o}$ is differentiable on $J$ and
   $$J_{o}'(t)=T_{o}^{\mathrm{ext}}(t)+I(t)-o'(t)\times P(t)=T_{o}(t)-o'(t)\times P(t)\qquad(t\in J);$$
3. **Centrality.** Suppose that for every $i<j$ and every $t\in J$ the
   evaluated pair force is parallel to $x_{i}(t)-x_{j}(t)$, that is, there is
   a real $\lambda_{ij}(t)$ with
   $$F_{ij}\bigl(t,x_{i}(t),x_{j}(t),w_{i}(t),w_{j}(t)\bigr)=\lambda_{ij}(t)\,\bigl(x_{i}(t)-x_{j}(t)\bigr).$$
   Then $I\equiv0$ on $J$, so
   $$J_{o}'(t)=T_{o}^{\mathrm{ext}}(t)-o'(t)\times P(t)\qquad(t\in J);$$
   if moreover $o$ is constant, then $J_{o}'=T_{o}^{\mathrm{ext}}$;
4. **Conservation.** If $o$ is constant and $T_{o}\equiv0$ on $J$ —
   equivalently $T_{o}^{\mathrm{ext}}\equiv-I$ there, by clause 1 — then
   $J_{o}$ is constant on $J$. In particular, if the evaluated pair forces
   are central (clause 3) and $T_{o}^{\mathrm{ext}}\equiv0$ on $J$ — the case
   of a model with no external forces — then $T_{o}\equiv0$ and $J_{o}$ is
   constant on $J$.

Clause 3 allows cancellation: the vanishing of $I$ is a hypothesis on the
evaluated pair forces and does not require centrality in general; the
companion page exhibits antisymmetric non-central pair forces whose internal
torque sum vanishes identically. No empirical content is claimed.
items.strategy: A direct computation: reindex the internal pair torques using antisymmetry to obtain the internal-torque identity, differentiate the angular momentum by the product rule to get the fixed and moving-origin balance, and discharge the centrality and vanishing-total-torque hypotheses.
items.physical_scope: The angular momentum balance of a model that declares the external-plus-pair presentation with antisymmetric pair forces: the internal torque sum is independent of the reference point and the balance about a possibly moving reference point carries the correction minus odot cross P; when the evaluated pair forces are central the internal torque sum vanishes; about a fixed point with vanishing external torque the angular momentum is constant. The result is conditional on the declared pair structure and centrality where invoked; it asserts no necessity of centrality and no measured value.

references.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 1.3, Eqs. (1.17)-(1.19), printed pages 6-7 (PDF pages 12-13): Ldot = sum_i r_i x F_i^ext + sum_{i<j}(r_i - r_j) x F_ij, with the internal term vanishing when F_ij is parallel to r_i - r_j

K. K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part CM: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), Section 1.3, Eqs. (1.31)-(1.38), chapter pages 8-10 (PDF pages 12-14): L = r x p, Ldot = tau, the total angular momentum, and the cancellation of the internal torque pairs when the mutual forces are central, with the external-torque balance

R. Fitzpatrick, Classical Mechanics (University of Texas at Austin), Non-Isolated Systems, Eqs. (42)-(44): the total angular momentum equation with the net external torque and the internal-torque cancellation

items.title: Power of the total force and the work-energy theorem: $K'=\mathcal P$ and $K(t_1)-K(t_0)=W([t_0,t_1])$ along a motion
items.statement:
Adopt the force model and one inertial frame of
[[def-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-momenta]]: masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, an
open configuration domain $Q$, the force map $F$ with the standing hypotheses
of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] clause (iii), and the quantities $w_{i}$,
$$K=\frac12\sum_{i}m_{i}\lVert w_{i}\rVert_{2}^{2},\qquad \mathcal P=\sum_{i}\bigl\langle F_{i}(t,x,w),\,w_{i}\bigr\rangle,\qquad W([t_{0},t_{1}])=\int_{t_{0}}^{t_{1}}\mathcal P(t)\,dt$$
along a curve family. Let $x:J\to Q$ be a **motion** of the model on an
interval $J$ with nonempty interior. Then:

1. $K$ is of class $C^{1}$ on $J$ and
   $$K'(t)=\mathcal P(t)\qquad(t\in J):$$
   the rate of change of the kinetic energy equals the power of the total
   force;
2. for all $t_{0}<t_{1}$ in $J$,
   $$K(t_{1})-K(t_{0})=\int_{t_{0}}^{t_{1}}\mathcal P(t)\,dt=W([t_{0},t_{1}]):$$
   the change of the kinetic energy equals the work of the total force.

No potential, no pair decomposition and no conservation hypothesis is used:
the identity is a consequence of the equation of motion alone, in the fixed
frame. The power and the work are frame-dependent (see clauses (iv) and (v)
of the frame-transformation item of this page); the mechanical energy
statement of the potential branch is the energy balance of this page.
items.strategy: A direct computation: differentiate the kinetic energy using the squared-norm product rule and the equation of motion to get K' equal to the power, then integrate with Newton-Leibniz for the work-energy theorem.
items.physical_scope: The work-energy identity of the force branch: along every motion the time derivative of the kinetic energy equals the power of the total force, and the change of kinetic energy over a time interval equals the work of the total force. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted equation of motion and uses no potential, no pair structure and no conservation hypothesis; it asserts no frame-independent value and no measured quantity.

references.title: K. K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part CM: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), Section 1.3, Eqs. (1.19)-(1.21), chapter pages 6-7 (PDF pages 10-11): T = m v^2/2, dT = p dot dr, and the work-energy principle T(r_B) - T(r_A) = integral of F dot dr along the trajectory

D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 1.3.2, Eq. (1.24) and the preceding display, printed page 8 (PDF page 14): the change of total kinetic energy equals the work integrals of the external and internal forces, sum_i integral F_i dot dr_i

items.title: Potential presentations of a force model, potential and mechanical energy, closed versus exact force fields, local potentials and equipotential level sets
items.statement:
Adopt the force model and one inertial frame of
[[def-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-momenta]], with configuration domain $Q$, time
window $I_{0}$ and force map $F$. Dimensions are read by [[def-cm01-units]]
and gradients are Euclidean ([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]); points of
$Q$ are written $x=(x_{1},\dots,x_{N})$ with $x_{i}\in\mathbb R^{3}$.

**(a) Potential representation of the force map.** A model **presents its
force map through a potential** when it declares a function
$$U:I_{0}\times Q\longrightarrow\mathbb R$$
of class $C^{2}$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), of
dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ (read in joules), with
$$F_{i}(t,x,v)=-\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)\qquad(i=1,\dots,N)$$
for every $(t,x,v)$ of the state domain; here $\nabla_{x_{i}}U$ is the
gradient of $u\mapsto U(t,x_{1},\dots,x_{i-1},u,x_{i+1},\dots,x_{N})$ at
$u=x_{i}$. More generally, a model may declare **residual forces**
$d_{i}:I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}\to\mathbb R^{3}$ of the standing
regularity of clause (iii) of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] and present
$$F_{i}(t,x,v)=-\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)+d_{i}(t,x,v);$$
the pair $(U,d)$ is then the model's presentation and
$F_{i}^{\mathrm{p}}:=-\nabla_{x_{i}}U$ is its **potential part**. The scalar
$U$ is a **potential energy** for the model's potential part; the framework's
earlier admission of potentials in [[post-cm02-interactions]] clause (iii) is
the special case $d\equiv0$. A model that presents its whole force map this
way with $d\equiv0$ is a **global potential model** (the term "conservative
model" is used only in this sense).

**(b) Potential and mechanical energy along a curve family.** For a curve
family $x:J\to Q$ of the model ([[def-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-momenta]]
clause (a)) define the **potential energy along the family** and the
**mechanical energy** by
$$U_{x}(t):=U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr),\qquad E(t):=K(t)+U_{x}(t)\qquad(t\in J),$$
with $K$ the kinetic energy of the definition. The potential part contributes
to the force field but not directly to $K$; $E$ is defined only along the
potential branch of the model, and along a motion it is the subject of the
energy balance of this page.

**(c) Normalization of the potential.** Let $c:I_0\to\mathbb R$ be
differentiable and put $\widetilde U:=U+c(t)$, retaining $C^2$ regularity
when a potential presentation of the standing class is required. The spatial
gradient is unchanged, so this presents the same potential part with the same
residual forces. The full converse is componentwise: if $\widetilde U$ and
$U$ are $C^2$ and have the same spatial gradient, then on each connected
component $C$ of the open set $Q$ there is a $C^2$ function
$c_C:I_0\to\mathbb R$ with
$$\widetilde U(t,x)-U(t,x)=c_C(t)\qquad(x\in C).$$
Here a connected component is a maximal connected subset of $Q$. For fixed
$t$, the difference is constant on every ball contained in $Q$: along any
segment in the ball its derivative is the vanishing spatial gradient paired
with the segment direction. The difference is consequently locally constant,
and on a connected component it is constant, since a value's level set and
its complement are both relatively open. Evaluating at any fixed point of
$C$ gives the $C^2$ regularity of $c_C$. Conversely, independent such functions
on the components give a $C^2$ potential with unchanged spatial gradient;
components of an open Euclidean set are open, because each sufficiently small
ball about one of their points is connected and lies in that component.
A single $c(t)$ describes every ambiguity precisely when the component
functions agree, in particular when $Q$ is connected. No agreement follows
from openness alone: on two disjoint balls the potentials $0$ and the function
equal to $0$ on one ball and $1$ on the other have the same force. Every
continuous motion on an interval remains in one component, so its energy
shifts by that component's $c_C(t)$ and its energy rate by $c_C'(t)$.
The representative is part of the model's declaration, and every energy
statement names it.

**(d) Closed and exact force fields.** A **time- and velocity-independent
configuration-space force field** is a $C^{1}$ map
$\varphi=(\varphi_{1},\dots,\varphi_{N}):Q\to(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$, where
$Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ is the open configuration domain and each
$\varphi_i(x)$ is the force on label $i$ at configuration $x$; its components
have force dimension. It represents a force map of the form
$F_i(t,x,v)=\varphi_i(x)$ on the model's state domain. This configuration-space
field is not in general an external single-label force: to identify its
$i$th component with an external map of [[post-cm02-interactions]] clause (i),
one must further require that it depend on $x_i$ alone, as in the declared
signature $F_i^{\mathrm{ext}}(t,x_i,v_i)$. Such a field is **closed** when
$\partial_{k}\varphi_{j}=\partial_{j}\varphi_{k}$ for all coordinate indices
$j,k\in\{1,\dots,3N\}$ at every point of $Q$, and **exact with potential
energy $U$** when $\varphi=-\nabla U$ for a $C^{2}$ function
$U:Q\to\mathbb R$; equivalently, the field $-\varphi$ is exact in the sense
of [[def-closed-and-exact-c1-vector-fields]] with potential $U$. The following
mathematical facts are used, with their proofs at the cited items:

1. every exact field is closed, by equality of mixed partial derivatives
   ([[def-closed-and-exact-c1-vector-fields]]);
2. on a star-shaped open domain every closed $C^{1}$ field is exact, by the
   Poincaré lemma ([[thm-poincare-lemma-for-star-shaped-domains]]);
3. beyond item 2 this item asserts **no** implication from closedness to
   global exactness: on a general open domain a closed field need not have a
   potential energy, and the criterion used by the framework is exactness as
   defined above.

Consequently the existence of a global potential energy on the model's
configuration domain is a property of the field on that domain, and a model
whose potential part is a merely closed field on a non-star-shaped domain is
not thereby a global potential model. The distinction is sharp: the
companion examples page carries a model on an annular domain whose force
field is smooth and closed, has nonzero circulation around a closed loop, and
therefore admits no global potential and no global conserved energy of the
form $K+U$, while item 2 provides a local potential and a locally conserved
energy on every star-shaped subpart of that domain.

**(e) Local potentials.** Let $V\subseteq Q$ be open and star-shaped with
respect to one of its points ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]) and let
$\varphi$ be closed on $V$. Then item 2 of (d) provides a $C^{2}$ potential
$U_{V}:V\to\mathbb R$ with $\varphi|_{V}=-\nabla U_{V}$: a **local potential**
of the field on $V$. On the restricted configuration domain $V$ the model
with force $-\nabla U_{V}$ is a global potential model, so the mechanical
energy $K+U_{V}$ is available along curve families in $V$; this is how a
potential is recovered from a merely closed field on a sufficiently small
star-shaped piece of the domain, with no claim of a global representative.

**(f) Equipotential level sets.** Let $U:Q\to\mathbb R$ be $C^{2}$, let
$c\in\mathbb R$ and suppose $U^{-1}(c)\neq\varnothing$ and $\nabla
U(x)\neq0$ for every $x\in U^{-1}(c)$; equivalently $c$ is a regular value of
$U$ and every point of the level set is a regular point
([[def-regular-and-critical-points-and-values]]). Then $U^{-1}(c)$ is an
embedded submanifold of $Q$ of dimension $3N-1$
([[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]],
[[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]). No such conclusion is made at a
level where $\nabla U$ vanishes somewhere on the level set, where the level
set may have singular points.

**(g) Status.** The potential, its normalization, the residual forces and the
declaration of a potential presentation are model data; the closed/exact
statements of (d)-(f) are cited mathematics about the declared field. This
item asserts no conservation law, no force law of nature and no measured
value.
items.strategy: A definition: it fixes potential presentations with residual forces, potential and mechanical energy along a curve family, the normalization under addition of a function of time, the closed/exact distinction for time- and velocity-independent fields with the cited Poincare result on star-shaped domains, local potentials on star-shaped subdomains and equipotential level sets.
items.physical_scope: The potential branch of the force model: a scalar potential representing the force map through the Euclidean gradient, with or without declared residual forces; the potential and mechanical energy along a curve family; the non-uniqueness of the potential under addition of a function of time; the distinction between closed and exact time- and velocity-independent force fields, with local potentials on star-shaped subdomains and the failure of global exactness on a punctured domain; and equipotential level sets. The item defines the branch and records cited mathematical facts; it asserts no conservation law, no measured value and no global potential for an arbitrary closed field.

references.title: K. K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part CM: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), Section 1.3, Eqs. (1.22)-(1.27) and footnote 15, chapter pages 7-8 (PDF pages 11-12): the potential (conservative) force F = -nabla U, the work of potential forces as U(A) - U(B), mechanical energy E = T + U, and the additive constant in U

D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 1.3.2, Eqs. (1.24)-(1.25) and the conservative-force conditions, printed page 8 (PDF page 14): conservative external and internal forces from potentials and the total potential energy V = sum_i V_i + sum_{i<j} V_ij

J. Lebl, Basic Analysis II, Section 9.3 Example 9.3.7 (path independence and the vortex field) and J.-B. Campesato, Poincare Lemma, sections 1-2: the closed field on the punctured plane with nonzero circulation is not exact, while closed fields on star-shaped domains are exact with the displayed radial potential

items.title: Mechanical energy balance for a potential presentation: $E'=\partial_tU$ plus the residual power, conservation for a static potential with no residual forces, and the integrated work form
items.statement:
Adopt the force model, one inertial frame, and the potential presentation of
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] clause (a): a $C^{2}$ potential
$$U:I_{0}\times Q\longrightarrow\mathbb R$$
of dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ and residual forces $d_{i}$ of the standing
regularity, with
$$F_{i}(t,x,v)=-\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)+d_{i}(t,x,v)\qquad(i=1,\dots,N)$$
on the state domain. Let $x:J\to Q$ be a **motion** of the model on an
interval $J$ with nonempty interior, write $\mathfrak d_{i}(t):=d_{i}(t,x(t),w(t))$
for the evaluated residual forces and
$$E(t):=K(t)+U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)$$
for the mechanical energy of the definition (clause (b)). Then:

1. $E$ is differentiable on $J$ and
   $$E'(t)=\partial_{t}U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)+\sum_{i}\bigl\langle\mathfrak d_{i}(t),\,w_{i}(t)\bigr\rangle\qquad(t\in J):$$
   the mechanical energy changes at the rate of the explicit time dependence
   of the potential plus the power of the residual forces;
2. if $\partial_{t}U\equiv0$ on $I_{0}\times Q$ and $\mathfrak d_{i}\equiv0$
   for every $i$ — the model is then a global potential model with the
   declared representative $U$ — then $E$ is constant on $J$;
3. for all $t_{0}<t_{1}$ in $J$,
   $$K(t_{1})-K(t_{0})=U\bigl(t_{0},x(t_{0})\bigr)-U\bigl(t_{1},x(t_{1})\bigr)+\int_{t_{0}}^{t_{1}}\Bigl[\partial_{t}U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)+\sum_{i}\bigl\langle\mathfrak d_{i}(t),w_{i}(t)\bigr\rangle\Bigr]dt,$$
   equivalently $W([t_{0},t_{1}])=U(t_{0},x(t_{0}))-U(t_{1},x(t_{1}))+\int_{t_{0}}^{t_{1}}\bigl[\partial_{t}U+\sum_{i}\langle\mathfrak d_{i},w_{i}\rangle\bigr]dt$:
   the work of the total force is the decrease of the potential energy plus
   the work of the explicit time dependence and of the residual forces.

The representative $U$ is the one declared by the model; replacing $U$ by
$U+c(t)$ changes $E$ by $c(t)$ and $E'$ by $c'(t)$, as recorded in
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] clause (c). The statement is read
in the fixed frame; no empirical content is claimed.
items.strategy: A conditional deduction: instantiate the mathematical work-energy balance for the potential presentation to obtain the mechanical-energy balance, apply the supplier's conservation clause for a static representative without residual forces, and integrate the power identity for the work form.
items.physical_scope: The mechanical energy balance of a model presented through a potential with declared residual forces: the derivative of the mechanical energy equals the partial time derivative of the potential plus the power of the residual forces; a time-independent potential with no residual forces conserves the mechanical energy along every motion; and the integrated form expresses the work of the total force through the change of the potential and the residual work. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted potential presentation, with the normalization of the potential carried along; it asserts no measured value and no conservation outside the stated hypotheses.

references.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 1.3.2, Eqs. (1.24)-(1.25), printed page 8 (PDF page 14): the total potential V = sum_i V_i + sum_{i<j} V_ij for conservative external and internal forces, and H = T + V conserved

K. K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part CM: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), Section 1.3, Eqs. (1.24)-(1.27), chapter pages 7-8 (PDF pages 11-12): the work of potential forces as U(A) - U(B), E = T + U, and conservation for conservative forces only, with non-conservative forces changing E

items.title: Transformation of the state quantities under a change of inertial frame: centre of mass, total momentum, kinetic energy, angular momentum, torque, power, work and mechanical energy
items.statement:
Adopt the force model and the notation of
[[def-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-momenta]], and let
$$F=\bigl(o,u,(e_{1},e_{2},e_{3})\bigr),\qquad F'=\bigl(o',u',(e_{1}',e_{2}',e_{3}')\bigr)$$
be two inertial frames with coordinates $(t,x)$ and $(t',x')$ related by
$$t'=t+b,\qquad x'=Rx+v\,t+a_{0},\qquad b\in\mathbb R,\ a_{0},v\in\mathbb R^{3},\ R\in SO(3)$$
([[pthm-cm01-galilean-kinematics]] clause 1,
[[def-cm-special-orthogonal-group]]). Let $x:J\to Q$ be a curve family of the
model in the first frame and let
$$\eta_{i}(t'):=R\,x_{i}(t'-b)+v\,(t'-b)+a_{0}\qquad(t'\in J+b)$$
be the description of the same worldlines in the second frame. Write
$\sigma_{i}(t):=F_{i}(t,x(t),w(t))$ and
$\Sigma(t):=\sum_{i}\sigma_{i}(t)$ for the evaluated total forces in the first
frame, and read the second frame's quantities from the description $\eta$
with the transferred force map $F_{*}$ of clause (vi) of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]]: $\tilde\sigma_{i}(t'):=F_{*i}(t',\eta(t'),\eta'(t'))$,
$\tilde P:=\sum_{i}m_{i}\eta_{i}'$,
$\tilde X:=M^{-1}\sum_{i}m_{i}\eta_{i}$,
$\tilde K:=\frac12\sum_{i}m_{i}\lVert\eta_{i}'\rVert_{2}^{2}$,
$\tilde J_{\tilde o}:=\sum_{i}(\eta_{i}-\tilde o)\times m_{i}\eta_{i}'$ and
$\tilde T_{\tilde o}:=\sum_{i}(\eta_{i}-\tilde o)\times\tilde\sigma_{i}$
for any $C^{1}$ reference curve $\tilde o:J+b\to\mathbb R^{3}$ (clause 3
uses the curve corresponding to $o$),
$\tilde{\mathcal P}:=\sum_{i}\langle\tilde\sigma_{i},\eta_{i}'\rangle$ and
$\tilde W([t_{0}',t_{1}']):=\int_{t_{0}'}^{t_{1}'}\tilde{\mathcal P}(t')\,dt'$
for $t_{0}'\le t_{1}'$ in $J+b$. Then, with all first-frame quantities read
at the corresponding time $t'-b$:

1. **Centre of mass and momentum.**
   $$\tilde X(t')=R\,X(t'-b)+v\,(t'-b)+a_{0},\qquad \tilde X'(t')=R\,V(t'-b)+v,\qquad \tilde P(t')=R\,P(t'-b)+M\,v\,;$$
2. **Kinetic energy.**
   $$\tilde K(t')=K(t'-b)+\bigl\langle v,\,R\,P(t'-b)\bigr\rangle+\frac12M\lVert v\rVert_{2}^{2};$$
3. **Angular momentum and torque.** For every $C^{1}$ reference curve
   $o:J\to\mathbb R^{3}$ of the definition, let
   $\tilde o(t'):=R\,o(t'-b)+v(t'-b)+a_{0}$ and
   $X_{o}(t):=M^{-1}\sum_{i}m_{i}(x_{i}(t)-o(t))=X(t)-o(t)$. Then
   $$\tilde J_{\tilde o}(t')=R\,J_{o}(t'-b)+\bigl(R\,X_{o}(t'-b)\bigr)\times(M\,v),\qquad \tilde T_{\tilde o}(t')=R\,T_{o}(t'-b),$$
   where $T_{o}(t):=\sum_{i}(x_{i}(t)-o(t))\times\sigma_{i}(t)$ is the
   evaluated total torque of the first frame about $o(t)$;
4. **Power and work.**
   $$\tilde{\mathcal P}(t')=\mathcal P(t'-b)+\bigl\langle R\,\Sigma(t'-b),\,v\bigr\rangle,$$
   and for every curve family and $t_{0}<t_{1}$ in $J$
   $$\tilde W\bigl([t_{0}+b,\,t_{1}+b]\bigr)=W([t_{0},t_{1}])+\int_{t_{0}}^{t_{1}}\bigl\langle R\,\Sigma(t),v\bigr\rangle\,dt.$$
   If in addition $x$ is a motion and the model invokes the pair presentation
   of [[post-cm02-interactions]] with the antisymmetry clause, then
   $\Sigma=P'$ along the motion by [[pthm-cm03-momentum-balance]], and
   $$\tilde W\bigl([t_{0}+b,\,t_{1}+b]\bigr)=W([t_{0},t_{1}])+\bigl\langle R\bigl(P(t_{1})-P(t_{0})\bigr),\,v\bigr\rangle;$$
5. **Potential and mechanical energy.** If the model is a global potential
   model of [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] clause (a) with
   potential $U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{2}$ and the second
   frame's model declares the **scalar transfer**
   $$U_{*}(t',y):=U\bigl(t'-b,\ R^{\mathsf T}(y_{1}-v(t'-b)-a_{0}),\dots,R^{\mathsf T}(y_{N}-v(t'-b)-a_{0})\bigr),$$
   then $U_{*}$ is $C^{2}$ on its open transferred domain,
   $F_{*i}(t',y,u)=-\nabla_{y_{i}}U_{*}(t',y)$ at corresponding data, and the
   mechanical energies of clause (b) of that definition satisfy
   $$\tilde E(t'):=\tilde K(t')+U_{*}\bigl(t',\eta(t')\bigr)=E(t'-b)+\bigl\langle v,\,R\,P(t'-b)\bigr\rangle+\frac12M\lVert v\rVert_{2}^{2}.$$

Whether the second frame's model uses the scalar transfer of clause 5 is a
modelling declaration; a model whose potential is not transferred by this rule
(for instance a background potential that selects a frame) is a different
model in the second frame, and no transformation law of $E$ is asserted for
it. No empirical content is claimed.
items.strategy: A direct computation: use the Galilean kinematic laws and the orthogonality of the rotation to transform centre of mass, momentum, kinetic energy, angular momentum, torque, power, work and, for the declared scalar transfer, the potential and mechanical energy, carrying the transferred force map of the force postulate.
items.physical_scope: The transformation laws of the model's mechanical quantities under a change of inertial frame: the centre of mass and centre-of-mass velocity transform affinely, the total momentum gains M times the boost velocity, the kinetic energy gains a cross term and the boost kinetic energy, the angular momentum and torque about corresponding C1 reference curves acquire the stated rotation and boost terms, and power and work transform according to the transferred force map of the force postulate, with the momentum-increment work form requiring a motion with the antisymmetric pair presentation; for a globally potential model whose potential is transferred by the scalar rule, the mechanical energy gains the same kinetic boost terms. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted frame, worldline and force laws; it asserts no invariance of these quantities and no measured value.

references.title: D. Tong, Dynamics and Relativity (Cambridge lecture notes, Lent 2013), Section 1.2.1, printed page 5 (PDF page 11): boosts x' = x + v t and rotations map inertial frames to inertial frames, and the coordinate velocity transforms with the boost velocity added

K. K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part CM: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), Section 1.1 point (v), chapter pages 2-3 (PDF pages 6-7): the transfer of the radius vector, velocity and acceleration between frames moving by relative translation, and the warning that rotations complicate the transfer

D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 1.2, printed pages 2-5 (PDF pages 8-11): the ten transformations relating inertial frames, comprising rotations, translations, boosts and time translation

items.title: Status audit and scope of the balance page: conditional conservation, open systems, frames, potential normalization and empirical boundaries
items.statement:
This remark records the status of the notions of the balance page. It is
bookkeeping: it asserts no law and no empirical claim, and every mathematical
statement it repeats is proved in the item cited.

**Adopted assumptions.** The force branch is the postulate
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]]: the force map with its standing continuity
and state-local-Lipschitz hypotheses, the equation of motion
$m_{i}\ddot x_{i}=F_{i}(t,x,\dot x)$ in every inertial frame, the additive
composition of declared force contributions and the transformation rule of a
force law under a change of inertial frame. The restricted interaction models
are the postulate [[post-cm02-interactions]]: the external-plus-pair
presentation, the optional antisymmetry and centrality clauses, the potential
branch and the gravitational branch. The linear drag model is the postulate
[[post-cm02-drag]].

**Defined objects.** The total mass, total momentum, centre of mass, relative
positions, angular momentum about a reference curve, total and external
torques, internal torque sum, kinetic energy, power and work are defined in
[[def-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-momenta]]; potential presentations, potential
and mechanical energy, the closed/exact distinction for time- and
velocity-independent force fields and equipotential level sets are defined in
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]. Motions and maximal motions are
[[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]].

**Conditional deductions.** The splitting of the kinetic sum and
$P=MV$ are [[pthm-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-kinetic-splitting]]. The momentum
balance and the centre-of-mass equation, under the antisymmetric
external-plus-pair presentation, are [[pthm-cm03-momentum-balance]]. The
angular-momentum balance about fixed and moving reference points, with the
centrality case, is [[pthm-cm03-angular-momentum-balance]]. The power identity
and the work-energy theorem are [[pthm-cm03-work-energy]]. The mechanical
energy balance and conservation for a static potential without residual
forces are [[pthm-cm03-energy-balance]]. The transformation laws of all these
quantities under a change of inertial frame are
[[pthm-cm03-frame-transformations]].

**Computed examples.** The companion page checks the laws on explicit data:
the two-body Hooke model with an exact circular relative motion (momentum,
angular momentum including the moving-origin correction, kinetic splitting,
energy conservation and the kinetic boost law), a driven one-dimensional
model with a time-dependent potential and a residual force (the balance, the
integrated work form and the normalization ambiguity), and the two
counterexamples recorded below.

**Deliberately not claimed on this page.** No conservation law holds without
its stated hypotheses: momentum conservation needs the antisymmetric pair
presentation and the vanishing of the total external force; angular-momentum
conservation needs a fixed reference point and the vanishing of the total
torque, with centrality only one sufficient condition (the companion
counterexample exhibits non-central pair forces whose torque sum cancels
identically); mechanical-energy conservation needs a global potential
presentation with a time-independent representative and no residual forces.
No theorem of this page asserts that any interaction of nature has the
required structure. No constraint reactions, no impulsive forces, no
variable-mass models and no measurements appear.
items.strategy: A scope remark: it audits the page status (adopted force and interaction posts, defined quantities, proved balances, computed examples), records the hypotheses each conservation statement needs, the centrality sufficiency, the closed-versus-exact distinction, the frame relativity, the open-system boundary and the empirical status of parameters.
items.physical_scope: A scope and status audit of the balance page: which objects are defined, which statements are conditional deductions from the force and interaction posts, which hypotheses each conservation statement needs, and which claims are deliberately not made; the frame dependence of the conserved quantities, the open-system boundary, the normalization of a potential, the local-versus-global potential distinction and the empirical status of model parameters. Bookkeeping and scope only; it asserts no law, no measurement and no conservation beyond the items it cites.

references.title: K. K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part CM: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), Section 1.3, chapter pages 8-10 (PDF pages 12-14): the caution that the conservation laws are first integrals of the equations of motion and introduce nothing new dynamically, and the central-force condition for the angular-momentum statement

D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 1.3, printed pages 5-9 (PDF pages 11-15): the third-law hypotheses behind the momentum and angular-momentum statements, the caution about momentum carried by omitted fields, and the conservative-force conditions behind energy conservation

title: Momentum, work and energy balances — Examples

items.title: A two-body Hooke model with an exact circular relative motion: momentum, kinetic splitting, moving-origin angular momentum, energy conservation and the kinetic boost law checked on explicit data
items.statement:
Fix the two-body model of [[post-cm02-interactions]] clause (iv) (the general
pair-potential example) with $N=2$, masses $m_{1}=m_{2}=m>0$, time window
$\mathbb R$, configuration domain $Q=\mathbb R^{6}$ (the potential below is
smooth everywhere, so no collision exclusion is needed), and the **Hooke pair
potential**
$$U(x_{1},x_{2}):=\frac12k\,\lVert x_{1}-x_{2}\rVert_{2}^{2},$$
with a declared **spring constant** $k>0$ of dimension $\mu\tau^{-2}$
([[def-cm01-units]]), so that $U$ has energy dimension. The force map is
$$F_{1}(x)=-k\,(x_{1}-x_{2}),\qquad F_{2}(x)=k\,(x_{1}-x_{2}),$$
the two negative gradients of $U$; it is linear in the positions and
independent of time and velocities, with
$\lVert F(x)-F(x')\rVert_{2}\le2k\lVert x-x'\rVert_{2}$, hence continuous and
state-locally Lipschitz with the uniform constant $2k$. The model therefore
satisfies the standing hypotheses of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] clause
(iii), it has no external forces ($F_{i}^{\mathrm{ext}}\equiv0$), and its
pair force is central: $F_{12}=-k(x_{1}-x_{2})$ is parallel to
$x_{1}-x_{2}$. It presents its force map through the global potential $U$ in
the sense of [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] clause (a).

Fix an oriented orthonormal triple $(e_{1},e_{2},e_{3})$ with
$e_{3}=e_{1}\times e_{2}$, a constant centre-of-mass velocity
$V\in\mathbb R^{3}$ of dimension $\ell\tau^{-1}$, and a length $R>0$,
and set $\omega:=\sqrt{2k/m}$ (dimension $\tau^{-1}$). Define
$$e(t):=\cos(\omega t)\,e_{1}+\sin(\omega t)\,e_{2},\qquad x_{1}(t):=Vt-\frac R2\,e(t),\qquad x_{2}(t):=Vt+\frac R2\,e(t)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R).$$
Then $x=(x_{1},x_{2})$ is the **unique maximal motion** of the model with the
datum $x_{1}(0)=-\frac R2e_{1}$, $x_{2}(0)=\frac R2e_{1}$,
$\dot x_{1}(0)=V-\frac R2\omega e_{2}$, $\dot x_{2}(0)=V+\frac R2\omega e_{2}$,
and along it:

1. the total momentum is $P=2mV$, constant, and the centre of mass is
   $X(t)=Vt$ with $V_{\mathrm{cm}}=V$;
2. the kinetic energy is $K=m\lVert V\rVert_{2}^{2}+\frac14mR^{2}\omega^{2}$,
   and its centre-of-mass/relative splitting holds with reduced mass
   $\mu=m/2$ and relative coordinate $r=x_{1}-x_{2}$;
3. the angular momentum about the origin is
   $J_{0}=\frac12mR^{2}\omega\,e_{3}$, constant, while for the moving
   reference curve $o(t)=\mathbf Wt$ with a constant velocity
   $\mathbf W\in\mathbb R^{3}$ of dimension $\ell\tau^{-1}$ and
   $\mathbf W\perp V$ one has
   $J_{o}'=-2m(\mathbf W\times V)$, in agreement with the moving-origin
   correction; this correction is nonzero when both $\mathbf W$ and $V$ are
   nonzero;
4. the mechanical energy is $E=m\lVert V\rVert_{2}^{2}+kR^{2}$, constant, and
   the power identity $K'=\mathcal P$ holds with
   $\mathcal P$ equal to the negative time derivative of the potential
   energy $\frac12k\lVert r\rVert_{2}^{2}$;
5. under the Galilean change to the centre-of-mass frame ($b=0$, $a_{0}=0$,
   $R_{\mathrm{rot}}=I_{3}$, $v_{\mathrm{boost}}=-V$) the transformed
   quantities are $\tilde P=0$, $\tilde K=\frac12kR^{2}$ and
   $\tilde E=kR^{2}$, in agreement with
   [[pthm-cm03-frame-transformations]] clauses 2 and 5.
items.strategy: A worked verification: define a two-body Hooke pair model with an explicit circular relative motion, verify the model hypotheses and the equations of motion, and compute momentum, splitting, moving-origin angular momentum, energy, power and the boosted kinetic and mechanical energies, comparing with the balance and transform laws.
items.physical_scope: A worked model check inside the two-body potential branch: for a declared Hooke pair potential with spring constant, mass, separation and centre-of-mass velocity data, the displayed circular relative motion is the unique maximal motion of the model, and along it the total momentum, centre-of-mass motion, kinetic splitting, angular momentum about fixed and moving reference points, mechanical energy and boosted kinetic energy take the values the balance theorems predict. The item asserts no measured value, models no physical spring and claims no empirical agreement.

references.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Sections 1.3.2-1.3.3, printed pages 8-9 (PDF pages 14-15): the two-body energy and momentum bookkeeping with a pair potential depending on the separation

K. K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part CM: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), Section 3.4, Eqs. (3.30)-(3.37), printed pages 40-42: the centre-of-mass and reduced-mass decomposition of the two-body kinetic energy

items.title: A driven one-dimensional model with a time-dependent potential and a residual force: the mechanical-energy balance, the integrated work form and the normalization ambiguity computed on explicit data
items.statement:
Work in the force branch of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with one label
$N=1$, mass $m>0$, time window $I_{0}=\mathbb R$ and configuration domain
$Q=\mathbb R$, and declare the **potential presentation** of
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] clause (a)
$$U(t,x):=\frac12\lambda\,t\,x^{2},\qquad d(t,x,v):=2ma+\lambda a\,t^{3},$$
where $a>0$ is a constant of dimension $\ell\tau^{-2}$ and $\lambda>0$ a
constant of dimension $\mu\tau^{-3}$, so that $U$ has dimension
$\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ and $d$ has the dimension of a force
([[def-cm01-units]]). Both maps are smooth; the force map of the model is
$F(t,x,v)=-\partial_{x}U(t,x)+d(t,x,v)=-\lambda tx+2ma+\lambda at^{3}$, and
the model is a potential presentation with residual force $d$ in the sense of
that definition.

The curve
$$x(t):=a\,t^{2}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R)$$
is a motion of this model, and with $K$, $\mathcal P$ of
[[def-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-momenta]] and
$E=K+U(t,x(t))$:

For the numerical clauses below, put $s:=t/(1\,\mathrm s)$; displayed energy,
power and work values include their SI units, and the interval $0\le s\le1$
means $0\le t\le1\,\mathrm s$.

1. on the interval $[0,1\,\mathrm s]$ the numerical data $m:=1\,\mathrm{kg}$,
   $a:=1\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-2}$, $\lambda:=1\,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm{s}^{-3}$
   give
   $$K(t)=2s^{2}\,\mathrm J,\qquad U(t,x(t))=\frac12s^{5}\,\mathrm J,\qquad E(t)=\left(2s^{2}+\frac12s^{5}\right)\mathrm J,\qquad E'(t)=\left(4s+\frac52s^{4}\right)\mathrm W,$$
   and the balance of [[pthm-cm03-energy-balance]] clause 1,
   $E'=\partial_{t}U(t,x(t))+d\,\dot x$, holds with
   $\partial_{t}U(t,x(t))=\frac12s^{4}\,\mathrm W$ and
   $d\,\dot x=(4s+2s^{4})\,\mathrm W$;
2. the power is $\mathcal P(t)=4s\,\mathrm W$, the work over $[0,1\,\mathrm s]$ is
   $W([0,1\,\mathrm s])=2\,\mathrm J$, and the work-energy theorem
   $K(1\,\mathrm s)-K(0)=W([0,1\,\mathrm s])$ holds; the integrated form of clause 3 of
   [[pthm-cm03-energy-balance]] holds as
   $2\,\mathrm J=-\frac12\,\mathrm J+\bigl(\frac1{10}+2+\frac25\bigr)\mathrm J$;
3. replacing $U$ by the equivalent potential
   $\tilde U(t,x)=U(t,x)+c(t)$ with
   $c(t):=-(1\,\mathrm J)\bigl(t/(1\,\mathrm s)\bigr)^{2}$
   (same force, different representative) gives
   $\tilde E(t)=E(t)+c(t)=\left(s^{2}+\frac12s^{5}\right)\mathrm J$ and
   $\tilde E'(t)=\left(2s+\frac52s^{4}\right)\mathrm W=\partial_{t}\tilde U(t,x(t))+d\,\dot x$,
   so the balance holds in the renormalized presentation with a different
   value and rate;
4. the model is driven and the energy is not conserved:
   $E(1\,\mathrm s)-E(0)=\frac52\,\mathrm J$
   in the first normalization, while the balance attributes the change to the
   explicit time dependence, $\int_{0}^{1\,\mathrm s}\partial_{t}U\,dt=\frac1{10}\,\mathrm J$, and
   the residual power, $\int_{0}^{1\,\mathrm s}d\,\dot x\,dt=\frac{12}{5}\,\mathrm J$, whose sum
   $\frac1{10}\,\mathrm J+\frac{12}{5}\,\mathrm J=\frac52\,\mathrm J$ is the energy change
   $E(1\,\mathrm s)-E(0)=\int_{0}^{1\,\mathrm s}E'\,dt$.
items.strategy: A worked computation: declare a one-dimensional potential presentation with a time-dependent potential and residual force, verify the quadratic motion, and evaluate the mechanical-energy balance, the power and work integrals and the renormalization shift on explicit numbers.
items.physical_scope: A worked computation in a declared one-dimensional potential presentation with an explicit time-dependent potential and residual force: the displayed quadratic curve is a motion of the model, and along it the mechanical-energy balance, the power identity, the integrated work form and the change of the energy under a time-dependent renormalization of the potential are computed from the model data. The item asserts no measured value and no conservation; the model is driven.

references.title: K. K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part CM: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), Sections 1.3-1.4, chapter pages 7-10 (PDF pages 11-14): the work-energy principle, potential forces, mechanical energy E = T + U and its failure to be conserved under non-conservative or explicitly time-dependent forcing

D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 1.3.2, printed page 8 (PDF page 14): the kinetic-energy change as the work of the forces and the conservative conditions required for an energy statement

items.title: Non-central antisymmetric pair forces with vanishing internal torque sum: the centrality clause is not necessary for angular-momentum conservation
items.statement:
In the force branch of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with the
external-plus-pair presentation and the antisymmetry clause (ii)1 of
[[post-cm02-interactions]], **if the internal torque sum
$\sum_{i<j}(x_{i}-x_{j})\times F_{ij}$ vanishes identically, then every pair
force $F_{ij}$ is central** (parallel to $x_{i}-x_{j}$).

Equivalently: centrality of the pair forces is necessary for the
internal-torque conclusion used by
[[pthm-cm03-angular-momentum-balance]].
items.strategy: A direct refutation: define a three-label model with constant antisymmetric non-central pair forces, verify it against the force branch, exhibit a motion, and prove the internal torque sum vanishes identically by a telescoping cancellation while the individual pair torques are nonzero, so angular momentum is conserved without centrality.
items.physical_scope: A counterexample inside the force branch: a three-label model with constant antisymmetric pair forces has non-central pair forces and yet its internal torque sum vanishes identically, so its total angular momentum about a fixed origin is constant along every motion even though the centrality hypothesis of the balance theorem fails. The item refutes only the claim that centrality is necessary for the internal-torque conclusion; it asserts no measured value and no conservation for general non-central models.

references.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 1.3.1, Eq. (1.19) and the surrounding discussion, printed pages 6-7 (PDF pages 12-13): the internal-torque sum as a sum over pairs, whose vanishing is discussed through the parallelism of each pair, with the bookkeeping by pairs of forces

K. K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part CM: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), Section 1.3, Eq. (1.37) and the pair cancellation argument, chapter pages 9-10 (PDF pages 13-14): the double sum of internal torques grouped into pairs and reduced by the central-force assumption

items.title: A closed (curl-free) model force field on an annular domain with no global potential energy: mechanical energy is available only locally
items.statement:
In the force branch of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with the potential
presentation of [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] clause (a):
**if a model's force field is time- and velocity-independent and closed
($\operatorname{curl} F=0$, equivalently $\partial_{j}F_{k}=\partial_{k}F_{j}$)
on its configuration domain, then the model is a global potential model; in
particular there is a global potential energy $U$ on the domain with
$F=-\nabla U$, the mechanical energy $K+U$ exists for every motion, and it is
conserved.**
items.strategy: A direct refutation: define a single-label model on a declared annular domain with a scaled vortex force field, verify the standing Lipschitz hypothesis by an explicit two-case estimate, compute closedness by the quotient rule and the nonzero circulation from the definition of the line integral, use the gradient theorem to exclude a global potential, and recover local potentials and local energy conservation on star-shaped subdomains.
items.physical_scope: A counterexample inside the potential branch: on a declared open annular configuration domain a smooth time- and velocity-independent force field is closed (curl-free) and yet has no global potential energy, so the model is not a global potential model, no global mechanical energy of the framework's form exists, and the energy-conservation hypothesis of the balance theorem cannot be replaced by closedness; on every star-shaped subdomain a local potential and a locally conserved mechanical energy do exist. The item asserts no measured value and no global conservation.

references.title: J. Lebl, Basic Analysis II, Section 9.3, Example 9.3.7 (the vortex field on the punctured plane) and J.-B. Campesato, Poincare Lemma, sections 1-2: the example of a closed field with nonzero circulation that is not exact, and the exactness of closed fields on star-shaped domains; the counterexample below recomputes the curl, the circulation and the obstruction from the definitions

D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 1.3.2, printed page 8 (PDF page 14): potential forces are defined by a global scalar potential, and the work of a potential force around a closed path is zero

K. K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part CM: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), Section 1.3, Eq. (1.24) and footnote 15, chapter page 7 (PDF page 11): the work of potential forces as the difference of U at the endpoints, hence zero on a closed path, with U defined via the gradient
